transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, it's probably not a huge deal. But, well, honestly... what made me come in is that I've been having a little bit of trouble at work. 

I'm an advertising sales agent, and we have these really long strategy meetings. And I just... I keep getting up during them. I know I'm supposed to just stay seated like everyone else, but I always end up popping up out of my chair. I try to make it look completely normal! Like, I'll just go refill my water, or I'll kind of pace over by the printer for a minute just to move. 

It's nothing disruptive, I promise. But I know it probably doesn't look incredibly professional to my manager when I can't just sit through the meeting. Does that make sense? I just thought I should maybe ask someone about it, if that's okay.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're not in meetings, like when you're at home or doing other activities?

Um, no, I don't really think so. At least, I haven't noticed it if I do. When I'm at home, I'm usually pretty... pretty normal, I think. 

I mean, I might tidy up or keep my hands busy while I watch TV or something, but everyone kind of does that, right? I don't think I'm pacing around my living room or doing anything weird. I really try to just relax when I'm off the clock, so I can be at my best for work the next day. 

I hope that's helpful? I just... I don't want to make it sound like I'm bouncing off the walls all the time, because I'm really not. It's mostly just those long work meetings where I feel like I'm doing something wrong. Is it okay that it's just happening at work?
Do you have difficulty paying attention during those long work meetings?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try my best to stay engaged, I promise. But... yeah, in those longer strategy meetings, or even if I'm just reading a long client brief, I'll start out completely focused. I really do. 

But then, after a few minutes, I'll sort of realize I've just been staring at the exact same slide, or the same paragraph, and I have absolutely no idea what the last point was. 

I always catch myself and try to get right back on track, though! I really don't want you to think I'm ignoring my coworkers or doing a bad job, because I care a lot about my work. It's just a little blip where my mind drifts. Does that sound like something a lot of people struggle with? I'm hoping it's pretty normal to zone out a little when things get long... right?
Do you feel anxious or stressed when you're in those long work meetings?

Oh, um, no. No, I don't think so. I actually really like my team, and the meetings themselves aren't really high-pressure or anything. I mean, my manager is great, so I definitely don't feel intimidated or... or anxious about being there. 

It's really just... I just get that little urge to move around, or my mind just kind of drifts, like I mentioned. But I'm not sitting there worrying or feeling stressed out at all. 

I hope I'm explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right. Is it... is it okay that it happens even when I'm completely relaxed?
Did you have trouble sitting still or paying attention when you were a kid in school?

Um, well... I guess I did have a little trouble with that when I was younger, yeah. I mean, it wasn't anything terrible! I was always a good kid, I promise. But... I do remember this happening way back, like, way before high school even. 

My elementary school teachers would always write on my report cards that I was really bright, which was nice! But they'd also say I... I rushed through my work a bit, or that I talked out of turn sometimes. And I guess I was a little forgetful with my homework, and my desk was always kind of a mess, just stuffed full of half-finished papers and things. 

I always meant to be organized and quiet, I really did. I just... I got a little too enthusiastic sometimes, I think? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student. A lot of kids are a little disorganized and talkative at that age, right? Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Have you ever had trouble keeping a job or getting along with friends because of your restlessness or difficulty paying attention?

Um... well, no, I wouldn't say I've ever had trouble getting along with friends! My friends are wonderful, and we get along really well. I try really hard to be a good friend, I promise. 

As for work... um, I definitely haven't ever lost a job or anything like that! I've always been able to keep my jobs. I do really care about doing good work for my clients. 

But... I guess, maybe recently... it has been mentioned just a tiny bit in my performance reviews? Nothing awful! Just... you know, some little notes about maybe missing small details. And... well, there was one client who... they were just a little frustrated because I missed something in an email thread, and they complained. 

It really wasn't a huge deal, but it did make me worry a little bit. I would hate to damage any accounts, because I really do try so hard to keep everyone happy and do my best. I just... I get a little scattered sometimes, I guess? I hope you don't think I'm a bad employee. It's just a little hiccup, right? A lot of people probably get minor complaints sometimes...?
Did you experience similar difficulties with restlessness and paying attention during your teenage years, after elementary school?

Um, well... I guess I didn't really notice it as much in middle school or high school. I mean, I don't think I did? I was really involved in a lot of clubs and things, so I was always pretty busy. 

I don't remember getting into any trouble for talking or moving around too much back then. I think I kind of figured out how to sit quietly by that point, you know? And I got decent grades! I really tried my best to stay on top of things. 

If I'm being completely honest, maybe I did still struggle a little bit with... just keeping track of all my assignments? But it wasn't anything major, I promise. I think a lot of teenagers probably have a hard time juggling all their classes, right? Did I answer that okay? I just don't want to make it sound like I was totally out of control or anything, because I really wasn't.
Do you still find yourself rushing through tasks or having trouble with organization in your daily life outside of work?

Um, well... I try really hard to keep things together at home, I really do! I'm definitely not a total mess or anything, I promise. But I guess... well, my organization can get just a little bit... creative sometimes? 

Like, the lines blur a bit between everything I'm juggling, and my system gets a little scattered. For example, my campaign notes for my accounts will somehow end up split between my emails, a bunch of sticky notes all over my desk, my physical planner, and just... so many random tabs open on my laptop at home. 

And then I sit there and... well, I guess I do waste a lot of time just trying to figure out what to do first instead of just starting the task. 

I always get everything done eventually, though! I just get a little overwhelmed trying to prioritize it all when it's spread out like that. I'm sure a lot of people have too many tabs open and use too many sticky notes these days, right? Everyone is just so busy. I hope that doesn't make my life sound too chaotic... is that the sort of thing you meant?
Do you currently have difficulty with impulsivity in your personal or professional life?

Um... impulsivity? Gosh, that sounds a little intense. I definitely don't do anything reckless or dangerous, I promise! I'm actually a very careful person. 

But, well... I guess if you mean just little things at work? Sometimes I can be a little bit... overly enthusiastic, maybe? Like, if one of my coworkers is working through a pitch deck, and I suddenly think of an idea for it... I have this habit where I'll just sort of pop over to their desk right then. Or, um, if they're in the middle of a conversation with someone else, I might accidentally interrupt them just to add my thought. 

I always mean well! I just get so excited to help, and I want to share the idea before it slips my mind. But... I guess, if I'm being honest, it probably could have waited. I always feel a little bad afterward, and I make sure to apologize! I try really hard to be polite and respectful of everyone's time, I really do. 

Does... does that sound like what you're asking about? I really hope my team doesn't think I'm rude... I just want to be a good collaborator.
Do you think you've grown out of the behaviors your elementary school teachers noted, or do you still find yourself exhibiting similar traits as an adult?

Um, well... I definitely don't think I'm running around the room or acting like a little kid anymore, I promise! I've definitely grown up a lot since elementary school. 

But I guess... well, some of the things we've been talking about, like the scattered notes and getting a little too eager to share ideas... I suppose those might be kind of similar? Just in a more grown-up way? 

If I really think about it, I guess I've been noticing these things a bit more recently. Like, it hasn't always been this much of a struggle. I'd say it's really been noticeably affecting me since I changed into advertising sales strategy... which was about two years and two months ago, I think? 

It's just a lot more independent work and juggling different accounts, so I think maybe it just requires a different kind of focus than my old role. I'm really trying my best to adapt, though! I want to do a good job. Do you think it's normal for a big career change to bring out some of these little quirks again? I just hope I don't sound like I'm failing at my job, because I'm really not.
Have you experienced any of these difficulties with restlessness, paying attention, or impulsivity consistently over the past few years, or have they varied over time?

Um... consistently? Gosh, I don't know if I'd say it's been a constant, everyday kind of thing. I really hope it doesn't sound like I've just been struggling non-stop this whole time! 

It definitely varies. Like, some weeks are completely fine, and I feel totally on top of everything at work and at home. But then... well, maybe if things get really busy, or if I have a lot of different accounts pulling me in different directions, that's when I might get a little more scattered or... or jumpy, I guess? 

Like I mentioned, before I took this specific role a couple of years ago, I don't think I really noticed it much at all. So I suppose it just fluctuates depending on how much I'm juggling at any given moment? 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer... I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I've definitely had plenty of really good, productive times too, I promise!
Have these difficulties with restlessness, paying attention, or impulsivity significantly impacted your daily life or relationships in any way?

Um, well... significantly impacted? That feels like a really strong word. I definitely don't want you to think my life is falling apart or anything! My relationships are great, my friends are wonderful, and I really do love my job. 

But... I guess, if I'm being totally transparent... there have been a couple of tiny hiccups at work. Nothing major, I promise! Just... well, my manager gently brought up a few things in my last performance review. Just about, you know, staying organized and making sure I'm fully present in meetings. 

And, um... there was this one little incident with a client. I guess they felt like I wasn't listening closely enough to their needs, and they actually complained. That honestly broke my heart a little bit, because I care so much about doing a good job for them. I was just so worried that I might accidentally damage an account, even though I'm trying my absolute hardest. 

I've been working really hard to fix it, though! I'm trying all sorts of new planners and reminders. I just... I really want to be seen as a reliable employee. Does that sound like the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope it doesn't make me sound like a terrible worker, because I really do put my all into it!
Have you experienced any symptoms of restlessness, difficulty paying attention, or impulsivity since you were a teenager?

Um, well... since I was a teenager? Gosh, I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, but... it actually goes back even further than that, I think? 

I know we touched on this a little bit earlier, but... yeah, my elementary school teachers used to leave these little notes on my report cards. They were always really nice about it! They'd say I was bright and enthusiastic, which was sweet of them. But they also mentioned that I tended to rush through things, or... or maybe talk out of turn sometimes when I got too excited. 

And, um, I guess I had a bit of a habit of forgetting my homework back then, too. My desk was always just... well, stuffed with half-finished papers and things. But I promise I wasn't trying to be a bad student! I really did want to do well, I just... I guess I had a lot of energy and a hard time keeping it all organized when I was little. 

Does that make sense? I know little kids can be messy and talkative, so I'm not sure if that's exactly what you're looking for... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline!
Have you ever had difficulty making or keeping friends because of your restlessness, inattention, or impulsivity?

Um, no, I don't think so! I mean, I really value my friendships, and I've always tried my best to be a good friend. I hope I am, anyway! 

I guess... well, maybe sometimes I might accidentally interrupt someone if I get really excited about a story they're telling, or... or I might be a tiny bit late to lunch because I lost track of time. But my friends are so incredibly understanding, and they know I never mean anything by it. I always apologize right away, and I make sure to let them know how much I appreciate them. 

So, no, I haven't really had trouble making or keeping friends. I'm actually really lucky to have a great group of people in my life! I hope that's a good thing to hear... I just really want to be a supportive person to the people I care about, you know?
Have you noticed these difficulties with restlessness and paying attention continuing into your adult life outside of work?

Um, outside of work? Honestly, I don't really think so! I mean, I try my absolute best to keep things running smoothly at home, and I think I do an okay job of it. 

I guess... well, I do like to stay busy on the weekends, so I might bounce around between a few different chores or hobbies, but it's never really felt like a difficulty. I might leave a book half-read on the coffee table, or have a tiny bit of clutter in my bedroom closet, but I always make sure my apartment looks nice and tidy, especially if I have company over! I'd hate for anyone to think I'm disorganized in my personal life. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I have any real trouble outside of the office. I really try to stay on top of my personal life and keep everything balanced. I hope that's a good sign? Like, that I'm managing things okay when I'm just being me at home?
Have you experienced any symptoms like restlessness, difficulty paying attention, or impulsivity since childhood that have continued into your adult life?

Um, well... I know we just talked about how I was as a kid, and I really hope I'm not confusing things! But as far as it being a real problem, like, something that actually makes things difficult? That hasn't been going on since childhood at all. 

I actually think I've managed pretty well for most of my life! It's really just... well, it's only been noticeably affecting me since I changed roles at work. I moved into advertising sales strategy about two years and two months ago, and... gosh, it's a wonderful opportunity, I'm so grateful for it! It's just a lot more self-directed than my old position. 

So, that's when I started feeling a little more... scattered, I guess? Like the restlessness and the trouble focusing really only became noticeable then. I really want to do a good job in this new role, and I'm trying so hard, I just... I hope it's okay that it hasn't been a lifelong struggle? Does that still make sense for what we're looking at?
Have you experienced any of these difficulties consistently since you were a child?

Um, well... I know I just said it only became a real problem recently with my new job, and I hope I'm not being contradictory! I just mean that it didn't feel like a *struggle* back then, you know? But, um, I guess if I really think about it... those kinds of things have been around for a long time. 

Actually, way before high school. I remember my elementary school teachers... they were always so sweet, but they would write on my report cards that I was bright but, um, maybe rushed through my work a little too fast? And that I talked out of turn sometimes, or forgot my homework. Oh, and my desk was always just stuffed with half-finished papers! 

But I was always a happy kid, and I really tried to be good! I just... I had a lot of energy, I guess. I hope it's okay that I didn't mention that right away? I just didn't want you to think I was a bad student or anything. I really did try my best! Does that help answer your question?
Have you experienced any of these difficulties, such as restlessness or trouble paying attention, consistently since you were a child, even if they weren't as noticeable at times?

Um, well... I know I just talked about this a little bit, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much! You're so patient to listen to me ramble. But yes, I guess if I look back, it really has been there since way before high school. 

I was just thinking about my elementary school teachers again. They were always so encouraging, but they did write on my report cards that... well, that I was a bright girl, but maybe I rushed through my assignments a bit? And they mentioned I talked out of turn sometimes, or would forget to bring my homework in. And oh my gosh, my desk... it was always just stuffed full of half-finished papers and things. 

I always felt so bad about it because I really wanted to be a good student and make my teachers happy! I just couldn't seem to slow down or keep everything organized, even back then. But I was always polite about it, I promise! I hope that makes sense? Like, that it's always kind of been there, even if I was trying my absolute hardest to hide it?
Have you experienced any difficulties with restlessness, paying attention, or impulsivity every year since you were a child?

Um, yes... I know we've been going back and forth on this, and I really hope I'm not being frustrating or confusing you! You've been so kind to keep clarifying it for me. 

But yes, if you mean every single year... I suppose it really has been a constant thing, even if I was managing it better at certain points. Like I mentioned before, it definitely started way before high school. Even in elementary school, my teachers—who were just the sweetest, by the way—would always write on my report cards that I was a bright girl, but that I rushed through things. And they'd gently point out that I talked out of turn or forgot my homework. And my poor desk was always just a disaster of half-finished papers! 

I really did try to be good and do what they asked every year, I just... I always had that same restless energy and trouble keeping it all together. I hope it's okay that I'm just now realizing it's been literally every year? I just always wanted to think I was doing better than I was, I guess. Does that finally give you the right answer?
Have you experienced any of these difficulties every year since childhood?

Oh, gosh... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm sounding like a broken record! I really hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're asking, you've been so incredibly patient with me. 

But yes, if we're looking at it year by year... it really was a constant thing, starting way before high school. Just like I was saying about my elementary school days, it was basically the exact same story on my report cards every single grade. My teachers would always write that I was a bright girl, but that I rushed through things, or talked out of turn, or forgot my homework. And I always had that same desk just overflowing with half-finished papers. 

I always felt so awful about it because I really, truly wanted to be good for them, and I tried so hard at the start of every school year to be perfectly organized! I just couldn't ever seem to keep it up. I hope that's what you were looking for? Please let me know if I'm not giving you what you need, I can try to think of different examples if that would be better!
